vignette: Three years ago, Talia was driving home from her shift at the downtown cybersecurity firm when a freight truck blew a tire and mounted the median. The impact threw her against the passenger door, crumpling the frame around her left side. Inside the wreckage, the acrid stench of scorched insulation filled the cabin, and a sharp, tearing sensation seized her ribs and shoulder that would not fade. When she closed her eyes, the visual memories of the twisted steel and shattered glass replayed with startling clarity. As the visual memories of the crumpled guardrail flashed behind her eyes, the memory itself cemented her belief that her body was fundamentally unreliable and that she was perpetually exposed to judgment. She began to feel entirely exposed to others, convinced that the bruising across her torso was so visible that colleagues would scrutinize her every movement. The sudden, unbidden smell of scorched wiring would make her certain that the world had been deeply unfair, leaving her with the lingering conviction that nothing would ever protect her again. Over the following months, the accident's aftermath bled into her sleep and her nights. She found it harder to feel safe at night than during the day, so she kept the bedroom lights dim but functional, scanning the hallway every few hours to verify that the locks held and the windows were secure. Her difficulty falling asleep stemmed from a need to stay alert, so she remained upright in the dark, convinced that drifting off would leave her defenseless. The belief that she was permanently exposed to judgment and that her own flesh could not be trusted turned every quiet evening into a state of hyperalertness. Her relentless hyperarousal and need to scan the environment constantly kept her nervous system primed, which meant every minor sensory shift immediately dragged the accident's images back to the forefront. The constant exhaustion from waking during the night to check whether she was safe only reinforced her fear that her body was fundamentally unreliable and that she would always be vulnerable to others' scrutiny. At her desk, Talia's daily routine became a carefully constructed fortress of control. She would sit for twelve hours straight, auditing network traffic logs, while deliberately avoiding all feelings that might spike her heart rate or bring her close to tears. When the office HVAC system kicked on, releasing a faint draft of dusty heat, her olfactory recall would trigger instantly, and she would immediately abandon the workstation to sit in her car, practicing memory erasure by reciting algorithmic code backwards until the pain recall in her left ribs subsided. Her conviction that her body was failing her and that the injustice around her was permanent drove her to systematically block out any emotion, while she also spent hours mentally dissecting the crash's cause. In her effort to suppress the crash, she would deliberately overload her senses with complex network diagrams, yet the very act of pushing the memories down only made the physical pain in her ribs flare up when she tried to rest. Because her threat responses kept her on high alert, she deliberately adopted avoidance strategies, refusing to process the event and instead burying her responses, which left her autonomic nervous system stuck in a perpetual state of readiness. By refusing to process the event and instead burying her responses, she left her nervous system in a state of permanent alarm, ensuring her waking alertness and hypervigilance never quieted. The accumulation of these habits had eroded her professional standing and isolated her from the few friends she had left. She could no longer sit through mandatory security briefings without her shoulders tensing against phantom impacts, and she had started declining client consultations because the flickering monitor light mimicked the flash of the impact. Seeking relief from a life governed by avoidance and dread, Talia finally walked into the clinic. She hoped someone could help her quiet the internal alarms, though she feared that if she ever let her guard down, the same unfairness that destroyed her car would leave her once more defenseless.
